text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: continuous-batching.streamer.us-west-2 p99 spike detected. p95=1.2s p99=8.7s (SLO: p99 < 5s). Routing error rate stable. Paging on-call.

Alex Cheng: on it. seeing a sudden tail on the contbatch path for streaming requests. Correlating with packer metrics now.

Alex Cheng: quick query run: `sum(rate(stream_latency_seconds_bucket{le=\"5.0\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(stream_requests_total[5m]))` — p99 jump starts ~ 2026-03-15T20:10 UTC.

Mira Patel: I pulled the dashboard — packing queue length up, avg batch size doubled for small-seq tenants, KV cache eviction spikes. Looks like mixed-seqlen requests are causing big padding and long scheduling waits.

Sana Rivera: customer-impact check: no broad 5xxs, a handful of customers report slow streaming (chat ux shows stalls). I've DM'd CSMs for the top 3 affected customers.

Jamie Torres: can we throttle large padders or force hetero segregation? Any quick surgical mitigation?

Alex Cheng: short-term plan: 1) reduce max_batch_size on streaming packer to 8 (was 32) 2) enable preemptive_shed for background-heavy queues 3) temporarily pin heavy-seq tenants to slow lane. I'll apply in dev first then prod canary.

Alex Cheng: applying change now to canary pool (packer-id=usw2-canary-3):
```bash
# runtime config update
curl -X POST https://config.internal/api/apply -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"service":"contbatch-packer","pool":"usw2-canary-3","max_batch_size":8,"pack_threshold_ms":12}'
```

ops-bot: deploy started for config change on usw2-canary-3. CI checks passed.

Mira Patel: canary metrics look promising: canary p99 down from 9.1s -> 2.4s in 90s. Queue length reduced by ~60%.

Sana Rivera: customer update ready: short note drafted to explain mitigation and request logs from affected tenants. sending after we confirm stability.

Jamie Torres: rolling to 20% of packers now (usw2-prod-{1..6}). watch for throughput regression.

Alex Cheng: rolling full pool with an adaptive rollout and auto-rollback on error rate increase >1%.

Alex Cheng: also toggled scheduler fairness mode to 'strict-seq' for a subset of hosts to avoid greedy packing across seq-length classes.

Mira Patel: logs show a transient increase in disk-backed KV reads during rollout, but no client errors. impacting tail only. can we evict stale KV entries more aggressively post-rollout?

Jamie Torres: noted. I'll bump kv.eviction_threshold to 0.6 after rollout.

incident-bot: NOTE: SLO watcher flagged in channel — next check in 5min.

Alex Cheng: after full rollout p99 stabilized at 3.1s across region — still above target but much improved. p95 fine. Continuing tuning: lower pack_threshold_ms to 8ms for streaming-only lanes, and set tenant isolation flag for top-10 heavy-seq customers.

Sana Rivera: tracking customer outreach: 3 customers affected, response windows 15-45min. no escalations yet.

Mira Patel: adding a short-term guardrail: requests that would pad >4x are routed to a 'low-latency' fast-path with smaller batch caps and no padding. config snippet:
```json
{"routing": {"fast_path": {"max_padding_ratio": 4, "max_batch_size": 6}}}
```

Jamie Torres: perf note: expect some token-cost increase for fast-path since less batching, but saves p99 and UX. Ops agreed.

ops-bot: rollout complete to 100% in usw2. No automatic rollbacks triggered.

Alex Cheng: post-mitigation checks: p99 trend now 2.8s -> holding ~3.0s. We'll keep an eye for next 30m. Authz and throughput normal.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: Severity 3 assigned. Handoff required in 50min.

Mira Patel: handing off to next oncall (Mira -> Jamie) in 45m. checklist: 1) monitor p99 trend and queue length 2) verify KV eviction change 3) confirm no client errors 4) finalize CCR (customer comms)

Jamie Torres: I've got it. I'll maintain the bridge and escalate to eng-runtime if p99 creeps >4.5s or error rate >0.5%.

Sana Rivera: I've sent customer-notify to affected accounts with ETA and mitigation steps. will update if any customer confirms resolution.

Alex Cheng: follow-ups for postmortem: - root cause hypothesis: mixed-seqlen padding amplifies scheduler latency plus KV churn; - action items: improve per-tenant seq-length prediction, add runtime packer fairness metrics, better canary sim for mixed workloads.

Mira Patel: documenting immediate action items in the runbook and creating tickets for tuning/observability.

oncall-bridge: Handoff ack — Jamie now primary oncall owner. Bridge remains open for 2h. :thumbsup: 

Jamie Torres: taking ownership. leaving playback notes in ops-runbook. tagging eng-runtime: @eng-runtime for follow-up on packing algorithm improvements.

Alex Cheng: thanks team. marking incident for 1-hr follow up and starting draft of incident timeline.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.

Sana Rivera: will update customer threads once we confirm 30m steady-state.

Jamie Torres: will keep this channel updated. closing Handoff in 2m.

ops-bot: reaction :white_check_mark: added by Alex Cheng
